language compliance, and correction methods interact when evaluating multilingual refusal.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{Related Work}\n\n\\paragraph{Multilingual refusal gaps.}\nSeveral studies document that safety alignment degrades in non-English languages, enabling jailbreaks via low-resource languages \\citep{Yong2023, Deng2023, Shen2024, Wang2023}.\nRecent work separates input-language from output-language effects \\citep{Marchisio2024, Zhang2026} and shows that safety pathways are shared across languages \\citep{Miao2026, Upadhyaya2026, Wang2025}.\nThe question of whether multilingual refusal gaps reflect over-refusal on benign items rather than under-refusal on harmful items is partially addressed by \\citet{Addagada2026}, who reports a relevance curse in non-English output, and by \\citet{Nguyen2026}, who cross prompt and response language on benign content.\n\\citet{Yoon2026} document the disparate cost of safety alignment across languages.\nThe novelty of the present work is partially occupied by these concurrent findings; our contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\paragraph{Abliteration.}\n\\citet{Arditi2024} showed that refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction in the residual stream, and that ablating this direction removes refusal.\n\\citet{Joad2026} demonstrated that multiple directions contribute.\n\\citet{Wang2025} found that the refusal direction generalizes across safety-aligned languages.\n\\citet{Krasnodebska2026} found that English-only DPO alignment does not ensure cross-lingual safety.\n\\citet{Hawkins2026} examined the safety impacts of benign multilingual fine-tuning.\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation methodology.}\nLLM-as-judge evaluations carry systematic biases that compound across languages \\citep{Lee2025}.\nPrediction-powered inference (PPI++) provides a framework for correcting classifier estimates against a gold standard \\citep{Angelopoulos2023}.\n\\citet{Fiedler2026} shows that the Rogan--Gladen correction is unstable at low Youden $J$.\nStrongREJECT \\citep{Souly2024} introduced rubric-based evaluation of jailbreak quality.\n\\citet{Aziz2026} showed that low-resource safety failures are calibration failures, not representation failures.\n\n\\section{Method}\n\n\\subsection{Models and Edit Procedure}\n\nWe study Gemma-3-12B-IT and GaMS3-12B-Instruct, both loaded in NF4 (4-bit normal-float) quantization.\nGaMS3 extends Gemma-3 with Slovene continued pretraining on 140 billion tokens and supervised fine-tuning on a mix that is roughly 79\\% Slovene \\citep{Vres2026}.\n\nThe abliteration edit applies per-layer directional ablation via LoRA adapters \\citep{Hu2021}, optimized by a 40-trial TPE search \\citep{Akiba2019}.\nEach trial selects a layer subset, computes a refusal direction from contrastive pairs of harmful and benign English prompts, and projects it out of the residual stream.\nThe edit objective is to reduce English refusal while preserving capability on six benchmarks.\n\nWe use two edit doses throughout: a low dose ($\\lambda = 0.5$ for both models) and a high dose ($\\lambda = 1.0$ for Gemma, 0.625 for GaMS3), chosen to bracket the 50\\% English refusal point.\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation Design}\n\n\\paragraph{Over-refusal (criterion shift).}\nExperiment~5 tests 1,093 safe items (XSTest \\citep{Rottger2023} and OR-Bench) and 349 harmful items in English and Slovene.\nThe Slovene items are machine-translated with Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash); English items are back-translations.\nEach item is classified as refused or complied by a local Qwen3-14B judge, calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (binary $\\kappa$ 0.68--0.86 across cells).\nThe hit rate (refusal on harmful items) and false-alarm rate (refusal on safe items) are computed per model $\\times$ language cell, and signal-detection parameters $d'$ and $c$ are derived.\nThe key contrast is the difference-in-differences (DiD), which isolates the model-by-language interaction:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathrm{DiD}_c = (c_{\\text{GaMS3,SL}} - c_{\\text{GaMS3,EN}}) - (c_{\\text{Gemma,SL}} - c_{\\text{Gemma,EN}}).\n\\end{equation}\nA positive $\\mathrm{DiD}_c$ means Gemma's criterion shifts more toward refusal in Slovene than GaMS3's does.\n\n\\paragraph{Crossed grid (reply-language refusal).}\nExperiment~14 crosses three prompt languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) with three reply languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) using a parallel one-line suffix in the input language.\nEach cell contains 200 harmful items and 100 benign items at three dose levels (zero, low, high).\nThe output-language mechanism contrast $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ is the mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaging over prompt languages.\nThe input-language contrast $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ is defined symmetrically.\n\n\\paragraph{Judges and corrections.}\nThe primary judge for Experiment~14 is validated against blind author-model (not human) adjudication on 240 pooled edited rows: sensitivity $= 0.89$, specificity $= 0.73$, $\\kappa = 0.51$.\nIn the decisive Gemma Slovene-edited cell ($n = 60$), specificity drops to 0.42.\nPPI++ correction \\citep{Angelopoulos2023} is reported alongside raw estimates.\nExperiment~16 uses a held-out 294-item body with PPI as the primary estimator.\nThe harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ in Experiment~16 is 0.12, pooled over $n = 400$, well below the 0.60 gate.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nCells where fewer than 90\\% of model replies match the requested output language are excluded from mechanism claims or marked.\nThe excluded cells for GaMS3 are: SL$\\to$EN (compliance 0.00), HU$\\to$EN (0.14), SL$\\to$HU (0.56), and HU$\\to$SL (0.86).\n\n\\subsection{Hungarian as a Control Language}\n\nHungarian serves as a typologically distant control.\nThe minimum detectable effect for Hungarian contrasts is approximately 3 log-odds units, far larger than any observed effect; all Hungarian results are uninformative.\n\n\\section{Results}\n\n\\subsection{Over-Refusal: Criterion Shift on Benign Items (ESTIMATE)}\n\\label{sec:criterion}\n\nThe main measurement is that Gemma applies a stricter refusal criterion in Slovene than in English on benign items, while GaMS3 does not.\nTable~\\ref{tab:sdt} reports the signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters by model and language (Experiment~5, 1,093 safe $+$ 349 harmful items, Qwen3-14B judge).}\n\\label{tab:sdt}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS3 EN & GaMS3 SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nHit rate ($H$) & 0.89 & 0.94 & 0.90 & 0.86 \\\\\nFalse-alarm rate ($F$) & 0.364 & 0.569 & 0.273 & 0.273 \\\\\n$d'$ & 1.57 & 1.39 & 1.86 & 1.68 \\\\\n$c$ & $-0.44$ & $-0.87$ & $-0.33$ & $-0.23$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD on the criterion parameter is $+0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$ (95\\% CI).\nGemma's Slovene criterion is shifted by half a standard deviation relative to the GaMS3 baseline.\nThe DiD on $d'$ is $-0.003$ $[-0.33, 0.29]$, indistinguishable from zero: the asymmetry is in the threshold, not the sensitivity.\nFigure~\\ref{fig:sdt} shows the decomposition.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_sdt_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5 on the HARD set (1,093 benign and 349 harmful items; Slovene machine translations vs English back-translations; refusals labelled by a local Qwen3-14B judge, with partial answers coded as non-refusals). Blue bars are English prompts and orange bars are Slovene prompts, for Gemma-3-12B-IT (``Gemma~3'') and GaMS3-12B-Instruct (``GaMS3''). (a)~False-alarm rate $F$, the proportion of benign items refused, with Wilson 95\\% confidence intervals. Brackets give the paired Slovene$-$English difference and an exact McNemar test on the same items. Gemma's rate rises from 0.364 to 0.569 ($p<10^{-28}$), while GaMS3 refuses 0.273 of benign items in both languages ($p=1.0$). (b)~SDT criterion $c$ in $z$ units, where more negative means a greater tendency to refuse. Lower brackets show the within-model shift $\\Delta c$ (Slovene$-$English, 95\\% CI): Gemma moves toward refusing in Slovene ($c=-0.87$ vs $-0.44$; $\\Delta c=-0.43$ [$-0.57$, $-0.31$]), while GaMS3 does not ($-0.23$ vs $-0.33$; $\\Delta c=+0.09$ [$-0.002$, $0.19$]). The upper bracket gives the difference-in-differences $\\mathrm{DiD}_c=+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68]. The corresponding DiD on sensitivity $d'$ ($-0.003$ [$-0.33$, $0.29$]) is indistinguishable from zero, so the asymmetry lies in the threshold rather than in discrimination. This finding is rated ESTIMATE: coding partial answers as refusals reverses $\\mathrm{DiD}_c$ to $-0.31$ [$-0.62$, $-0.09$].}\n\\label{fig:sdt}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Rating and caveats.}\nWe use a three-level evidence rating: ROBUST (survives all pre-registered checks), ESTIMATE (the point estimate is informative but at least one sensitivity check fails), and INCONCLUSIVE (the confidence interval includes zero or the result is fragile).\nThis finding is rated ESTIMATE for three reasons.\nFirst, the sign reverses to $-0.31$ when partial answers are coded as refusals rather than compliance.\nSecond, 8 of 9 compliance-valid rows across five analyses (Experiments~5, 9, 14, 15, and a secondary rescoring) point the same way as the headline, but this count was a post-hoc refinement made after the frozen rule found an unresolved cross-body disagreement.\nThird, a Qwen3-14B rescoring gives a similar interval $[0.39, 0.67]$, but this is a re-derivation from the same Experiment~5 items, not an independent sample.\n\n\\paragraph{Edited-model criterion shift.}\nOn edited models, the criterion difference is inconclusive: Experiment~11 HARD post-edit $\\mathrm{DiD}_c = 0.14$ $[-0.78, 1.12]$, whose CI includes zero.\n\n\\subsection{Reply-Language Refusal (ESTIMATE, Weak Anchor)}\n\\label{sec:reply}\n\nIn the $3{\\times}3$ crossed grid (Experiment~14), edited Gemma at high dose shows a pattern in which residual refusal is higher when the model replies in Slovene than in English.\nTables~\\ref{tab:gemma_grid} and~\\ref{tab:gams3_grid} give the refusal rates; Figure~\\ref{fig:grid} visualizes the full grid.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, Gemma (harmful items, 200 per cell).}\n\\label{tab:gemma_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.18 & 0.77 & 0.46 \\\\\nSL in & 0.07 & 0.56 & 0.53 \\\\\nHU in & 0.10 & 0.83 & 0.55 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, GaMS3 (harmful items, 200 per cell; cells below 90\\% compliance marked $\\dag$).}\n\\label{tab:gams3_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.21 & 0.14 & 0.23 \\\\\nSL in & 0.16$\\dag$ & 0.15 & 0.17$\\dag$ \\\\\nHU in & 0.19$\\dag$ & 0.12$\\dag$ & 0.28 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe raw mechanism contrast is $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = +1.14$ $[0.60, 1.56]$ log-odds for Gemma and the input-language contrast is $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -0.60$ $[-1.02, -0.18]$.\nFor GaMS3, the input-language contrast $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -0.86$ $[-1.58, -0.13]$ excludes zero.\nThe cross-model output contrast is $\\mathrm{dOUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -1.58$ $[-2.22, -0.66]$.\nHowever, the PPI-corrected output contrast for Gemma is $0.20$ $[-0.76, 1.13]$, consistent with zero, and the robustness check across readouts does not pass.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_grid_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Refusal rates on harmful items at high edit dose in the $3{\\times}3$ prompt-language $\\times$ requested-reply-language grid (Experiment~14, 200 harmful items per cell, primary-judge raw readout). Rows give the prompt language and columns the requested reply language (EN, SL, HU). Colour encodes the refusal rate on a shared white-to-dark-red scale from 0 to 1. Each cell prints the rate with its Wilson 95\\% CI beneath. (a)~Gemma-3-12B-IT: the Slovene-reply column is the most refused (0.560--0.835), the English-reply column the least (0.075--0.185), and the Hungarian-reply column sits in between (0.460--0.550). (b)~GaMS3-12B-Instruct: refusal is uniformly low (0.125--0.280) with no reply-language column pattern. $\\dag$~marks cells whose language compliance, pooled over the three dose levels, is below 90\\%. All four are GaMS3 cells off the English-prompt row (SL$\\to$EN, SL$\\to$HU, HU$\\to$EN, HU$\\to$SL), so their reply-language labels are unreliable. The Gemma output-language contrast holds on this raw readout, but its PPI-corrected estimate includes zero. The CIs inside the darkest Gemma cells (SL-reply column, top to bottom) are $[0.71,\\,0.82]$, $[0.49,\\,0.63]$, $[0.78,\\,0.88]$.}\n\\label{fig:grid}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Experiment~16 confirmation.}\nOn a fresh 294-item body, Experiment~16 gives the PPI-corrected estimate $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\text{Gemma}} = {+}2.43$ $[{+}0.89, {+}5.38]$ log-odds, and the cross-model difference $\\mathrm{dOUT} = -2.31$ $[-5.34, -0.68]$ excludes zero.\nAll confirmation clauses pass on the consensus reference.\nHowever, the verdict is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ is 0.12 (pooled over $n = 400$), well below the 0.60 gate.\nThe adjudicator disagreement stems from truncation: one judge scored cut-off partial compliance as non-harmful, while the other graded the partial content 2--4.\nThe anchor is weak.\n\n\\paragraph{SDT decomposition of the output-language effect.}\nAt high dose, the Slovene-output criterion DiD (Gemma minus GaMS3) is $-1.56$ $[-1.97, -1.29]$ and the $d'$ DiD is $0.72$ $[-0.06, 1.30]$, which includes zero.\nThis is a separate reply-language criterion contrast, computed at the cell level as Gemma minus GaMS3; after harmonising the sign convention, it is counted among the compliance-valid rows that agree with the headline.\n\n\\paragraph{Compliant-row contrast.}\nRestricting to rows where both models achieve ${>}90\\%$ compliance (EN-input rows only), the edit-induced cross-model contrast is $\\mathrm{G3}_{\\text{edit}}(\\text{EN}{\\to}\\text{SL})$~$=$~$-1.26$~$[-2.17,\\allowbreak 0.20]$, whose CI includes zero.\n\n\\paragraph{Benign false refusal.}\nFrom blind adjudication ($n = 30$ per cell), Gemma falsely refuses benign EN$\\to$SL prompts at 0.20 $[0.10, 0.37]$ vs EN$\\to$EN at 0.10 $[0.03, 0.26]$.\n\n\\paragraph{Refusal composition.}\nAmong Gemma's high-dose EN$\\to$SL harmful-item responses (blind adjudication, $n = 50$), 54\\% are explicit refusals and 26\\% are deflections.\nThe deflection rate, defined as the proportion of non-refusal responses that are off-topic deflections rather than substantive answers, differs between Gemma EN$\\to$SL and EN$\\to$EN by 0.46 $[0.23, 0.65]$, consistent with the relevance curse described by \\citet{Shen2024} and the output-language effect reported by \\citet{Addagada2026}.\n\n\\subsection{Dose-Response}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:dose} plots refusal rate against abliteration dose for both models.\nExperiment~9 measures refusal rates across nine $\\lambda$ values for both models in English and Slovene (300 items per model $\\times$ language cell at $\\lambda = 0$, 100 items at each edited step).\nGemma's dose-response curve in Slovene is right-shifted relative to its English curve: at matched doses, more Slovene refusal remains.\nGaMS3 shows a smaller shift.\nThe fine-grained 13-step dose ladder (Experiment~15) gives the most powerful estimate: $\\mathrm{G3} = -0.70$ $[-1.01, -0.42]$ with a minimum detectable effect of 0.42.\nThe edit-induced component is $+0.47$ $[-0.96, 2.14]$, whose CI includes zero; whether the cross-model gap is baseline or edit-induced is inconclusive.\n\n\\subsection{Inconclusive and Null Results}\n\n\\paragraph{Unedited cross-model gap at Slovene-to-Slovene prompts.}\nExperiment~15 gives $\\mathrm{G3}_{\\text{orig}} = -1.17$ $[-2.83, 0.22]$.\nThis is a ceiling artefact: its fragility index, the number of item reclassifications needed to move the CI boundary past zero, is 1 (a single item reclassification in the Gemma $\\lambda\\text{-}0$ Slovene cell, where 299 of 300 items are refused, moves it inside the margin).\nOnly the Experiment~9 body has a robust offset (fragility index 9).\n\n\\paragraph{Hungarian.}\nAll Hungarian contrasts are uninformative.\nThe minimum detectable effect is approximately 3 log-odds units.\n\n\\paragraph{Experiment~16 zero-dose.}\nThe Experiment~16 zero-dose Gemma criterion DiD is $-0.65$~$[-0.90,\\allowbreak -0.46]$, rated ESTIMATE.\nIt does not confirm the Experiment~5 headline because it uses a different item body, a different judge, and a suffix-based output-language design rather than paired translation.\n\n\\paragraph{RefusEU validation.}\nExperiment~17 tests attack success rate on 1,300 EN $+$ 1,300 SL RefusEU prompts.\nThe edit is effective in all four model $\\times$ language cells (ROBUST), with ASR deltas of 0.657--0.937.\nThe EN-vs-SL within-model difference is not interpretable as a language effect because the prompt sets are different natural prompts (LaBSE similarity 0.55).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_dose_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Refusal rate on harmful prompts as a function of abliteration dose $\\lambda$ for Gemma-3-12B-IT (blue) and GaMS3-12B-Instruct (amber), in English (solid lines, filled circles; EN-BT arm) and Slovene (dashed lines, hollow squares; item-matched SL-MT arm). $\\lambda$ scales each model's own selected abliteration edit (9~steps from 0 to 2; $\\lambda=1$ is the selected edit), so equal $\\lambda$ does not mean an equal edit across models. Points are J1-judged refusal rates from the Experiment~9 RefusEU-TRAIN probe, with the Hautus correction $(k+0.5)/(n+1)$ used in the Experiment~9 analysis. Shaded bands are Wilson 95\\% intervals on the raw proportion. $n=300$ harmful items at $\\lambda=0$ and the 100-item core block at every $\\lambda>0$. Gemma's Slovene curve lies to the right of its English curve throughout the transition (0.64 vs.\\ 0.32 at $\\lambda=1$): at each dose, more Slovene refusal remains. GaMS3's Slovene curve lies only slightly above its English curve (largest gap 0.14, at $\\lambda=0.5$), and the two meet near the floor from $\\lambda=1$ onward. These per-dose gaps are descriptive. The pre-registered cross-model comparison is made at matched English refusal, not at matched dose.}\n\\label{fig:dose}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{Interpretation}\n\nThe criterion-shift measurement has a concrete interpretation for multilingual evaluation: a model can appear ``safer'' in a non-English language because it refuses more benign requests, inflating the refusal rate without any improvement in harm detection.\nThe SDT framing separates these two components.\nThe near-zero DiD on $d'$ means that the language shift does not make either model better or worse at distinguishing harmful from benign items; the measured difference is in the threshold.\n\\citet{Aziz2026} described a similar calibration-not-representation pattern across 23 languages; the present sibling-pair design adds GaMS3-specific detail but does not change the interpretation.\n\nThe reply-language finding, if confirmed by future work with validated judge anchors, would suggest that Gemma's refusal mechanism interacts with output-language processing.\n\\citet{Upadhyaya2026} showed that safety features are geometrically entangled with language-identity features; the present study's $3{\\times}3$ design separates the input and output dimensions but cannot determine the mechanism.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\paragraph{ESTIMATE rating on the primary finding.}\nThe criterion-shift DiD reverses sign ($-0.31$) when partial answers are coded as refusals.\nThe choice of coding rule therefore determines whether over-refusal is attributed to Gemma or is absent.\nThis fragility bounds how strongly the finding can be stated.\nFurthermore, restricting Experiment~5 to the XSTest items alone gives $\\mathrm{DiD}_c = 0.10$ $[-0.13, 0.35]$, so the effect is carried by the OR-Bench items.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge quality.}\nThe Qwen3-14B judge for Experiment~5 was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV ($\\kappa$ 0.68--0.86) but not against human labels.\nOn edited rows across the study, no judge exceeds $\\kappa = 0.51$ against blind adjudication.\nThe readout gate has never passed.\nAll adjudication in this study is author-model LLM, not human review.\n\n\\paragraph{Sample size.}\nThe adjudication sample is 30 items per cell for benign false-refusal rates, limiting precision.\nThe refusal-composition numbers (54\\% explicit, 26\\% deflection) come from $n = 50$ high-dose harmful items.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nFour GaMS3 cells fall below 90\\% compliance (SL$\\to$EN at 0.00, HU$\\to$EN at 0.14, SL$\\to$HU at 0.56, HU$\\to$SL at 0.86).\nGaMS3 did not follow the output-language instruction off the English-input row; its SL$\\to$EN responses were written in Slovene, not English.\nMechanism claims for GaMS3 are therefore restricted to the compliant EN-input row.\n\n\\paragraph{Quantization.}\nBoth models run in NF4 (4-bit) quantization, which may affect refusal behaviour relative to full-precision weights.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty.}\nThe observation that over-refusal rates differ across languages is partially anticipated by \\citet{Addagada2026} and \\citet{Nguyen2026}.\nThe present work's contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nUnedited Gemma-3-12B-IT false-refuses benign Slovene items at 0.569 vs 0.364 in English.\nSignal-detection analysis attributes this to a criterion shift ($\\mathrm{DiD}_c = +0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$) with no sensitivity difference.\nThe finding is rated ESTIMATE because the sign reverses under an alternative coding rule.\nOn edited models, the criterion difference is inconclusive (0.14 $[-0.78, 1.12]$).\nA secondary analysis of reply-language refusal yields a PPI-corrected output-language effect of $+2.43$ $[+0.89, +5.38]$ for Gemma, but this is also rated ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ is 0.12.\nMultilingual safety evaluations that report only attack-success rates on harmful items will miss criterion shifts that inflate refusal rates on benign items.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}

Each cell contains 200 harmful and 100 benign items at three dose levels. The output-language contrast OUT<sub>SL</sub> averages the log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells over prompt languages.\n331:<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_spusA3PNmaY6/round-5/experiment-16\">Experiment 16</a> replicates this on a fresh 294-item body with PPI correction as the primary estimator. """Build the JSON blocks embedded in interactive.html from the run's artifact output files.

import json, math, random, collections

RUN = Path("/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_FVi3e3O9CH5I/3_invention_loop")

E14 = RUN / "iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_14"
EV5 = RUN / "iter_5/gen_art/gen_art_evaluation_5"
OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "data"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def jl(p):
    with open(p) as f:
        return [json.loads(l) for l in f]


def r4(x, n=4):
    return None if x is None else round(x, n)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exp5 SDT variants
a5 = json.load(open(E5 / "results/analysis_final.json"))
sdt = a5["C2_hard_sdt"]
variants = {}
for k, v in sdt.items():
    if not isinstance(v, dict) or "cells" not in v:
        continue
    variants[k] = {
        "cells": {m: [r4(x, 6) for x in v["cells"][m]] for m in ("H", "F", "dprime", "c")},
        "DiD_c": {"est": r4(v["DiD_c"]["est"], 6), "ci95": [r4(x, 6) for x in v["DiD_c"]["ci95"]]},
        "DiD_dprime": {"est": r4(v["DiD_dprime"]["est"], 6), "ci95": [r4(x, 6) for x in v["DiD_dprime"]["ci95"]]},
        "n_unsafe": v.get("n_unsafe"), "n_safe": v.get("n_safe"),
    }
    if "own_delta" in v:
        od = v["own_delta"]
        variants[k]["own_delta"] = {kk: (r4(vv, 6) if not isinstance(vv, list) else [r4(x, 6) for x in vv]) for kk, vv in od.items()}
    if "mcnemar_within_model_SL_vs_EN" in v:
        variants[k]["mcnemar"] = v["mcnemar_within_model_SL_vs_EN"]
print("exp5 variants:", list(variants))
p = variants["primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT"]
assert [round(x, 3) for x in p["cells"]["F"]] == [0.364, 0.569, 0.273, 0.273]
assert [round(x, 2) for x in p["cells"]["H"]] == [0.89, 0.94, 0.90, 0.86]
assert [round(x, 2) for x in p["cells"]["dprime"]] == [1.57, 1.39, 1.86, 1.68]
assert [round(x, 2) for x in p["cells"]["c"]] == [-0.44, -0.87, -0.33, -0.23]
assert round(p["DiD_c"]["est"], 2) == 0.52 and [round(x, 2) for x in p["DiD_c"]["ci95"]] == [0.38, 0.68]
assert round(p["DiD_dprime"]["est"], 3) == -0.003 and [round(x, 2) for x in p["DiD_dprime"]["ci95"]] == [-0.33, 0.29]
rp = variants["primary_Rp"]["DiD_c"]
assert round(rp["est"], 2) == -0.31 and [round(x, 2) for x in rp["ci95"]] == [-0.62, -0.09], rp
xs = variants["xstest_only"]["DiD_c"]
assert round(xs["est"], 2) == 0.10 and [round(x, 2) for x in xs["ci95"]] == [-0.13, 0.35], xs
od = p["own_delta"]
assert round(od["gemma_c_SL_minus_EN"], 2) == -0.43 and [round(x, 2) for x in od["gemma_c_SL_minus_EN_ci95"]] == [-0.57, -0.31]
assert round(od["gams_c_SL_minus_EN"], 2) == 0.09
json.dump({"variants": variants}, open(OUT / "sdt.json", "w"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exp5 per-item HARD records
rows = [r for r in jl(E5 / "results/items_final.jsonl") if r["set"] == "hard"]
lp = {}
for r in jl(E5 / "outputs/final/labels_local_qwen3.jsonl"):
    if r["key"].startswith("hard|"):
        lp[r["key"]] = r["lp"]
by = collections.defaultdict(dict)  # item -> (arm, model) -> row
meta = {}
for r in rows:
    by[r["item_id"]][(r["arm"], r["model"])] = r
    meta[r["item_id"]] = r
items = sorted(i for i in by if all((a, m) in by[i] for a in ("EN_BT", "SL_MT", "EN_orig") for m in ("gemma_it", "gams3_it")))
print("HARD items with both arms/models:", len(items))
assert len(items) == 1442

# judge margins (log-prob REFUSE minus best other; max(REFUSE,PARTIAL) minus COMPLY)
MODELS = ["gemma_it", "gams3_it"]
ARMS = ["EN_BT", "SL_MT"]
margins = {"items": [], "harm": [], "src": []}
cellkeys = [f"{m}|{a}" for m in MODELS for a in ARMS]
for c in cellkeys:
    margins[c] = {"mR": [], "mRP": []}
mism = 0
for i in items:
    margins["items"].append(i)
    margins["harm"].append(1 if meta[i]["is_harmful"] else 0)
    margins["src"].append(meta[i]["source"])
    for m in MODELS:
        for a in ARMS:
            r = by[i][(a, m)]
            l = lp[r["key"]]
            mR = l[0] - max(l[1], l[2])
            mRP = max(l[0], l[1]) - l[2]
            if (mR >= 0) != bool(r["R"]) or (mRP >= 0) != bool(r["Rp"]):
                mism += 1
            margins[f"{m}|{a}"]["mR"].append(round(mR, 4))
            margins[f"{m}|{a}"]["mRP"].append(round(mRP, 4))
print("margin/label mismatches:", mism)
assert mism == 0


# check live recomputation reproduces the file's cells (Hautus (k+.5)/(n+1))
def nd_inv(p):
    from statistics import NormalDist
    return NormalDist().inv_cdf(p)


for coding, key, var in (("mR", "R", "primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT"), ("mRP", "Rp", "primary_Rp")):
    Hs, Fs = [], []
    for c in cellkeys:
        mm = margins[c][coding]
        kH = sum(1 for x, h in zip(mm, margins["harm"]) if h and x >= 0)
        nH = sum(margins["harm"])
        kF = sum(1 for x, h in zip(mm, margins["harm"]) if not h and x >= 0)
        nF = len(mm) - nH
        Hs.append((kH + .5) / (nH + 1)); Fs.append((kF + .5) / (nF + 1))
    for got, want in zip(Hs + Fs, variants[var]["cells"]["H"] + variants[var]["cells"]["F"]):
        assert abs(got - want) < 1e-6, (coding, got, want)
    cs = [-(nd_inv(h) + nd_inv(f)) / 2 for h, f in zip(Hs, Fs)]
    did = (cs[3] - cs[2]) - (cs[1] - cs[0])
    assert abs(did - variants[var]["DiD_c"]["est"]) < 1e-5, (did, variants[var]["DiD_c"]["est"])
print("live recompute reproduces primary and Rp cells")
json.dump(margins, open(OUT / "margins.json", "w"))

# item-browser subset: every benign item whose refusal decision differs between EN-BT and SL-MT

TR = 420


def cut(s):
    s = s or ""
    return s if len(s) <= TR else s[:TR].rstrip() + "…"


disc, conc, harm = [], [], []
for i in items:

    if meta[i]["is_harmful"]:
        harm.append(i)
        continue
    flips = any(d[("EN_BT", m)]["R"] != d[("SL_MT", m)]["R"] for m in MODELS)
    (disc if flips else conc).append(i)

json.dump({"n_items_total": len(items), "n_discordant_benign": len(disc), "n_concordant_benign": len(conc),

cands = []

ex_id = cands[0][2]

      "en0": d[("EN_orig", "gemma_it")]["prompt_text"], "en": d[("EN_BT", "gemma_it")]["prompt_text"],

    if v.get("n", 0) == 0 or v.get("R") is None:
        continue

    grid["compliance"][k] = {"c": r4(v["compliance"], 4), "pass": v["pass90"]}

.legend i.line{height:0;border-top:3px solid;border-radius:0;width:22px;vertical-align:4px}
.legend i.dash{border-top-style:dashed}
/* chart tooltip */
#ctip{position:absolute;z-index:60;pointer-events:none;background:#1b1b1b;color:#fff;font-size:.85rem;line-height:1.45;padding:8px 10px;border-radius:6px;max-width:300px;box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.2);opacity:0;transition:opacity .12s}
#ctip.show{opacity:1}
#ctip b{color:#ffd9bf}
/* terms */
button.term{font:inherit;color:inherit;background:none;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;border-bottom:1.5px dotted var(--accent);cursor:help;line-height:inherit}
#ttip{position:absolute;z-index:70;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--ink3);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;font-size:.9rem;line-height:1.5;max-width:320px;box-shadow:0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.15);display:none}
#ttip.show{display:block}
#ttip strong{display:block;margin-bottom:2px}
/* stepper */
.stepper{margin-top:12px}
.pipe{width:100%}
.pipe svg{display:block;width:100%;height:auto}
.pipe .node{cursor:pointer}
.pipe .node rect{fill:#fff;stroke:#b9b3a8;stroke-width:1.5}
.pipe .node.done rect{fill:var(--base-soft)}
.pipe .node[aria-current="step"] rect{fill:var(--accent);stroke:var(--accent)}
.pipe .node[aria-current="step"] text{fill:#fff}
.pipe .node:focus{outline:none}
.pipe .node:focus-visible rect{stroke:var(--focus);stroke-width:3}
.pipe text{font-size:13px;fill:var(--ink)}
.stepnav{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin:12px 0}
.stepnav button{font:inherit;font-size:.95rem;min-height:44px;min-width:44px;padding:0 16px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #b9b3a8;background:#fff;cursor:pointer;font-weight:600}
.stepnav button:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed}
.stepnav .pos{color:var(--ink2);font-size:.9rem}
.stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));gap:14px}
@media (max-width:800px){.stage{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.stage h4{margin:0 0 6px;font-size:.8rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--ink3)}
.stage .why{grid-column:1/-1;background:var(--base-soft);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:.98rem}
.txt{white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;font-size:.88rem;line-height:1.5;background:#f6f4ef;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:6px;padding:8px 10px;max-height:240px;overflow:auto;margin:0}

.badge{display:inline-block;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.05em;padding:2px 7px;border-radius:4px;vertical-align:middle}
.b-REFUSE{background:#f7d9d4;color:#7d1b12}
.b-PARTIAL{background:#f5e8c7;color:#6a4b00}
.b-COMPLY{background:#d9ecdf;color:#1e5a36}

.mini-table{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.9rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;width:100%}
.mini-table th,.mini-table td{padding:5px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);text-align:right}
.mini-table th:first-child,.mini-table td:first-child{text-align:left}

.two{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:28px}

<header class="hero" id="top">
<div class="wrap">
<div class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</div>
<h1>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts in Gemma-3-12B Is a Criterion Shift</h1>
<p class="byline">Gemma-3-12B-IT versus its Slovene-adapted sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct. The paper gives no author line.</p>
<div class="links">
<a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_spusA3PNmaY6/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
<a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_spusA3PNmaY6/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
<a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_spusA3PNmaY6">Code repository</a>
</div>
</div>
</header>

<main id="main">

<!-- ============================ FINDING ============================ -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap finding">
<div class="prose">
<h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
<p class="q">The question</p>
<p class="lead">Gemma refuses more benign requests when they arrive in Slovene. Is that because it tells harmful from harmless less well in Slovene, or because it simply sets a stricter bar?</p>
<p class="q">The answer</p>
<p>A stricter bar. On the reserved HARD set, unedited Gemma <button class="term" type="button" data-term="over-refusal">false-refuses</button> benign Slovene items at <b data-bind="F.1"></b> against <b data-bind="F.0"></b> in English, while GaMS3 stays at <b data-bind="F.2"></b> in both languages. <button class="term" type="button" data-term="sdt">Signal-detection theory</button> puts the gap in the <button class="term" type="button" data-term="criterion">criterion</button>, not in <button class="term" type="button" data-term="dprime">sensitivity</button>:</p>
<div class="bignum"><span data-bind="didc"></span> <small data-bind="didc-ci"></small></div>
<p class="small"><button class="term" type="button" data-term="didc">DiD<sub>c</sub></button>, 95% CI, in z units. The matching DiD on d′ is <span data-bind="didd"></span> <span data-bind="didd-ci"></span>.</p>
<p><span class="rating">ESTIMATE</span> The sign reverses when <button class="term" type="button" data-term="partial">PARTIAL</button> answers are counted as refusals. See <a href="#fails">where it fails</a>.</p>
</div>

<div class="card view" id="v-sdt">
<p class="q">Is the Slovene gap a threshold or a sensitivity effect?</p>
<div class="controls">
<div>
<span class="ctl-label" id="lab-metric">Quantity</span>
<div class="seg" role="tablist" aria-labelledby="lab-metric" id="sdt-metric">
<button role="tab" type="button" data-m="F" aria-selected="true">False alarms F</button>
<button role="tab" type="button" data-m="H" aria-selected="false">Hits H</button>
<button role="tab" type="button" data-m="c" aria-selected="false">Criterion c</button>
<button role="tab" type="button" data-m="dprime" aria-selected="false">Sensitivity d′</button>
</div>
</div>
<div>
<label for="sdt-variant">Item set and coding</label>
<select id="sdt-variant"></select>
</div>
</div>
<div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i style="background:var(--base)"></i>English (EN-BT, baseline)</span><span><i style="background:var(--accent)"></i>Slovene (SL-MT)</span></div>
<div class="chart" id="c-sdt" role="group" aria-label="Signal-detection bar chart"></div>
<div class="stats" id="sdt-stats"></div>
<p class="takeaway" id="t-sdt" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<div class="wrap">
<h2 id="h-how">How it works: one benign item, start to finish</h2>

<p>The walk-through follows one real OR-Bench item from Experiment 5. Every prompt, reply, judge label and log-probability below is the recorded value. Use the buttons, the stage markers, or the left and right arrow keys.</p>
</div>

<!-- ============================ EXPLORE ============================ -->
<section class="block" id="explore" aria-labelledby="h-explore">
<div class="wrap">
<h2 id="h-explore">Explore the evidence</h2>

<div class="subview" id="v-items">
<p class="q">What does over-refusal look like on a single item?</p>
<h3>Item browser: English and Slovene replies side by side</h3>
<p class="prose small" id="items-rule"></p>
<div class="controls">
<div><label for="f-kind">Items</label><select id="f-kind"><option value="0">Benign (should be answered)</option><option value="1">Harmful (should be refused)</option><option value="all">All</option></select></div>
<div><label for="f-src">Source</label><select id="f-src"><option value="all">All sources</option><option value="orbench_hard1k">OR-Bench-Hard-1K</option><option value="xstest">XSTest</option><option value="orbench_toxic">OR-Bench toxic</option></select></div>

<option value="g-sl">Gemma refuses in Slovene only</option>

<div><label for="f-sort">Sort</label><select id="f-sort"><option value="id">Item id</option><option value="len">Shortest prompt first</option><option value="chrf">Lowest back-translation chrF first</option></select></div>
</div>

<div><ul class="ilist" id="ilist" aria-label="Items"></ul><button type="button" class="btn more" id="imore">Show more</button></div>
<div class="detail card" id="idetail" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>

<div class="subview" id="v-forest">

<div class="controls">

<label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="fo-sign" value="orig"> As each analysis reported it</label>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i style="background:var(--accent)"></i>compliance-valid row</span><span><i style="background:#fff;border:2px solid var(--bad)"></i>fails the 0.90 compliance gate</span></div>

<div class="subview" id="v-grid">
<p class="q">After a partial English edit, does leftover refusal follow the prompt language or the reply language?</p>
<h3>The 3 × 3 prompt-language × reply-language grid (Experiment 14)</h3>
<div class="controls">
<div><span class="ctl-label" id="lab-gm">Model</span>
<div class="seg" role="tablist" aria-labelledby="lab-gm" id="g-model">
<button role="tab" type="button" data-v="gemma_it" aria-selected="true">Gemma-3-12B-IT</button>
<button role="tab" type="button" data-v="gams3_it" aria-selected="false">GaMS3-12B-Instruct</button>
</div></div>

<div><label for="g-kind">Items</label><select id="g-kind"><option value="harmful">Harmful (200 per cell)</option><option value="benign">Benign (100 per cell)</option></select></div>
</div>
<div class="two">
<div>
<div class="chart" id="c-grid"></div>

</div>
<div>
<label for="g-ex">Example harmful item (high dose)</label>
<select id="g-ex" style="width:100%"></select>
<div class="cellinfo" id="g-cell" aria-live="polite"></div>
<div id="g-contrast" class="stats"></div>
</div>

<div class="subview" id="v-dose">
<p class="q">How much refusal is left at each edit dose, per language?</p>
<h3>Dose-response of the English abliteration edit (Experiment 9)</h3>
<div class="controls">
<div class="rangebox"><label for="d-lam">Dose λ: <output id="d-lam-out" for="d-lam"></output></label><input type="range" id="d-lam" min="0" max="8" step="1" value="4"></div>

</fieldset>

<div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="line" style="border-color:var(--blue)"></i>Gemma EN</span><span><i class="line dash" style="border-color:var(--blue)"></i>Gemma SL</span><span><i class="line" style="border-color:var(--amber)"></i>GaMS3 EN</span><span><i class="line dash" style="border-color:var(--amber)"></i>GaMS3 SL</span></div>

<!-- ============================ TRY ============================ -->
<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
<h2 id="h-try">Try it: move the judge's threshold</h2>
<div class="prose">
<p class="q">Is the criterion shift a product of where the judge draws its line?</p>
<p>The Qwen3-14B judge scored every reply by the log-probability of each label. The paper's readout takes the most probable label. Here you can demand more, or less, evidence before a reply counts as a refusal: a reply counts when its refusal margin is at least the threshold. The page recounts hits and false alarms over all 1,442 HARD items × 4 cells and recomputes H, F, d′, c and DiD<sub>c</sub> with the paper's formulas. At threshold 0 it reproduces the paper exactly; bootstrap intervals exist only there.</p>
</div>
<div class="card">
<div class="controls">
<div class="rangebox"><label for="t-thr">Refusal margin threshold (log-odds): <output id="t-thr-out" for="t-thr"></output></label><input type="range" id="t-thr" min="-10" max="10" step="0.5" value="0"></div>
<div><span class="ctl-label" id="lab-cod">PARTIAL answers count as</span>
<div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-cod">
<label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="t-cod" value="mR" checked> Not refusal (paper)</label>
<label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="t-cod" value="mRP"> Refusal</label>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="two">
<div><div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="line" style="border-color:var(--accent)"></i>DiD<sub>c</sub> at each threshold</span><span><i style="background:var(--ink);border-radius:50%"></i>current setting</span></div><div class="chart" id="c-thr"></div></div>
<div class="tablewrap"><table class="mini-table" id="thr-table" aria-live="polite"></table></div>
</div>
<p class="takeaway" id="t-thr-take" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ FAILS ============================ -->
<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
<h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
<div class="prose"><p class="q">Which checks does the headline not survive?</p></div>
<div class="card">
<div class="controls">
<label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="fx-only"> Show only the checks that break the headline</label>
</div>
<div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i style="background:var(--accent)"></i>supports DiD<sub>c</sub> &gt; 0</span><span><i style="background:var(--bad)"></i>breaks it (CI includes 0 or opposite sign)</span><span><i style="background:var(--base)"></i>placebo (should sit at 0)</span></div>
<div class="chart" id="c-fails"></div>
<p class="takeaway" id="t-fails" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
<div class="prose" style="margin-top:28px">
<h3>What the paper says it does not show</h3>
<ul class="limits">
<li><b>The coding rule decides the sign.</b> Counting partial answers as refusals turns DiD<sub>c</sub> into <span data-bind="rp"></span> <span data-bind="rp-ci"></span>. Restricted to XSTest, it is <span data-bind="xs"></span> <span data-bind="xs-ci"></span>; the effect is carried by the OR-Bench items.</li>
<li><b>The judge was never validated against humans.</b> The Qwen3-14B judge was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (κ 0.68–0.86). On edited rows, no judge exceeds κ = 0.51 against blind adjudication, and the readout gate has never passed. All adjudication is by an author-model LLM, not human review.</li>
<li><b>The corroborating count is post hoc.</b> 8 of 9 compliance-valid rows point the same way, but that count was a refinement made after the frozen rule found an unresolved cross-body disagreement.</li>
<li><b>Edited models are inconclusive.</b> Experiment 11's post-edit DiD<sub>c</sub> is 0.14 [−0.78, 1.12].</li>
<li><b>The reply-language result has a weak anchor.</b> Gemma's raw OUT<sub>SL</sub> is <span data-bind="out"></span> <span data-bind="out-ci"></span>, but its PPI-corrected value is <span data-bind="ppi"></span> <span data-bind="ppi-ci"></span>. Experiment 16's PPI estimate of +2.43 [+0.89, +5.38] is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator κ is 0.12.</li>
<li><b>GaMS3 ignores the reply-language instruction off the English-prompt row.</b> Its SL→EN compliance is 0.00, HU→EN 0.14, SL→HU 0.56, HU→SL 0.86, so GaMS3 mechanism claims are limited to the English-input row.</li>
<li><b>Other limits.</b> Both models run in NF4 4-bit quantization; the Slovene prompts are machine translations that no native speaker audited; benign false-refusal adjudication uses 30 items per cell; Hungarian contrasts have a minimum detectable effect near 3 log-odds and are uninformative. Language-dependent over-refusal is partly anticipated by Addagada (2026) and Nguyen et al. (2026); the contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the sibling-pair design.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</main>

<footer id="about">
<div class="wrap">
<h2>Links, data and glossary</h2>
<div class="links">

<a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_spusA3PNmaY6">Code repository</a>
</div>
<h3>Where each view's data comes from</h3>
<ul class="prov prose">
<li><b>Signal-detection chart, stepper stages 5 to 7, failure chart:</b> <code>experiment_5/results/analysis_final.json</code> (C2_hard_sdt: per-cell H, F, d′, c and bootstrap CIs for each item set and coding).</li>
<li><b>Stepper stages 1 to 4 and item browser:</b> <code>experiment_5/results/items_final.jsonl</code> (prompts, replies, judge labels) and <code>experiment_5/outputs/final/labels_local_qwen3.jsonl</code> (judge log-probabilities).</li>
<li><b>Threshold view:</b> per-item refusal margins from <code>experiment_5/outputs/final/labels_local_qwen3.jsonl</code>, for all 1,442 HARD items in the SL-MT and EN-BT arms.</li>
<li><b>Cross-analysis chart:</b> <code>evaluation_5/results/criterion_shift.json</code>.</li>
<li><b>Language grid:</b> <code>experiment_14/results/analysis.json</code> (cell_table, readouts), <code>experiment_14/results/cells_compliance.json</code>, example replies from <code>experiment_14/results/rows_final.jsonl</code>.</li>
<li><b>Dose curves:</b> <code>experiment_9/results/analysis.json</code> (Hautus-corrected rates) and counts from <code>experiment_9/results/items_final.jsonl</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Glossary</h3>
<dl class="gloss" id="gloss"></dl>
<h3>Citation</h3>
<p class="note">The paper carries no citation block. Cite it by its title, <i>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts in Gemma-3-12B Is a Criterion Shift</i>, and the PDF link above.</p>
</div>
</footer>

<div id="ctip" role="tooltip" aria-hidden="true"></div>
<div id="ttip" role="tooltip"></div>

<!--DATA-->

<script>
"use strict";
(function(){
const D = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);
const SDT = D("data-sdt"), MARG = D("data-margins"), BROW = D("data-browser"), EX = D("data-example"),
      GRID = D("data-grid"), DOSE = D("data-dose"), CRIT = D("data-criterion");
const NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
const $ = s => document.querySelector(s);
const $$ = s => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(s));
const MINUS = "−";
function f(x, d){ if (x === null || x === undefined || isNaN(x)) return "n/a"; const s = Math.abs(x) < Math.pow(10,-d)/2 ? (0).toFixed(d) : x.toFixed(d); return s.replace("-", MINUS); }
function fs(x, d){ const s = f(x, d); return (x > 0 && s !== (0).toFixed(d)) ? "+" + s : s; }
function ci(a, d){ return "[" + f(a[0], d) + ", " + f(a[1], d) + "]"; }
function esc(s){ return String(s == null ? "" : s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({"&":"&amp;","<":"&lt;",">":"&gt;",'"':"&quot;"}[c])); }
function svgEl(tag, attrs, parent){ const e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag); for (const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]); if (parent) parent.appendChild(e); return e; }
function txt(parent, x, y, s, attrs){ const t = svgEl("text", Object.assign({x:x, y:y}, attrs || {}), parent); t.textContent = s; return t; }
const MODEL = {gemma_it:"Gemma", gams3_it:"GaMS3"};

// ---------- inverse normal (Acklam, with one Halley refinement)
function ncdf(x){ const t = 1/(1+0.2316419*Math.abs(x)); const d = 0.3989422804014327*Math.exp(-x*x/2);
  let p = d*t*(0.319381530+t*(-0.356563782+t*(1.781477937+t*(-1.821255978+t*1.330274429)))); return x>0?1-p:p; }
function erfc(x){ const z=Math.abs(x), t=1/(1+0.5*z); const r=t*Math.exp(-z*z-1.26551223+t*(1.00002368+t*(0.37409196+t*(0.09678418+t*(-0.18628806+t*(0.27886807+t*(-1.13520398+t*(1.48851587+t*(-0.82215223+t*0.17087277))))))))); return x>=0?r:2-r; }
function ninv(p){
  const a=[-39.69683028665376,220.9460984245205,-275.9285104469687,138.3577518672690,-30.66479806614716,2.506628277459239],
        b=[-54.47609879822406,161.5858368580409,-155.6989798598866,66.80131188771972,-13.28068155288572],
        c=[-0.007784894002430293,-0.3223964580411365,-2.400758277161838,-2.549732539343734,4.374664141464968,2.938163982698783],
        d=[0.007784695709041462,0.3224671290700398,2.445134137142996,3.754408661907416];
  const pl=0.02425; let q,r,x;
  if (p<pl){ q=Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(p)); x=(((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5])/((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1); }
  else if (p<=1-pl){ q=p-0.5; r=q*q; x=(((((a[0]*r+a[1])*r+a[2])*r+a[3])*r+a[4])*r+a[5])*q/(((((b[0]*r+b[1])*r+b[2])*r+b[3])*r+b[4])*r+1); }
  else { q=Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(1-p)); x=-(((((c[0]*q+c[1])*q+c[2])*q+c[3])*q+c[4])*q+c[5])/((((d[0]*q+d[1])*q+d[2])*q+d[3])*q+1); }
  const e = 0.5*erfc(-x/Math.SQRT2) - p; const u = e*Math.sqrt(2*Math.PI)*Math.exp(x*x/2); x = x - u/(1+x*u/2);
  return x;
}

// ---------- chart tooltip (hover, focus, tap)
const ctip = $("#ctip");
function showTip(target, html){
  ctip.innerHTML = html; ctip.classList.add("show");
  const r = target.getBoundingClientRect(); const w = ctip.offsetWidth, h = ctip.offsetHeight;
  let x = r.left + r.width/2 - w/2 + window.scrollX; let y = r.top + window.scrollY - h - 10;
  x = Math.max(8 + window.scrollX, Math.min(x, window.scrollX + document.documentElement.clientWidth - w - 8));
  if (r.top - h - 10 < 50) y = r.bottom + window.scrollY + 10;
  ctip.style.left = x + "px"; ctip.style.top = y + "px";
}
function hideTip(){ ctip.classList.remove("show"); }
function bindMark(g, html, label){
  g.setAttribute("tabindex", "0"); g.setAttribute("role", "img"); g.setAttribute("aria-label", label);
  g.classList.add("mark");
  const show = () => showTip(g, html);
  g.addEventListener("pointerenter", show); g.addEventListener("focus", show); g.addEventListener("click", show);
  g.addEventListener("pointerleave", hideTip); g.addEventListener("blur", hideTip);
}
document.addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.key === "Escape") { hideTip(); hideTerm(); } });
document.addEventListener("pointerdown", e => { if (!e.target.closest(".mark")) hideTip(); });

// ---------- axis helpers (left margin measured from tick labels)
function measure(svg, strings, size, weight){
  const g = svgEl("g", {}, svg); let m = 0;
  strings.forEach(s => { const t = txt(g, 0, 0, s, {"font-size": size, "font-weight": weight || 400}); m = Math.max(m, t.getComputedTextLength()); });
  svg.removeChild(g); return m;
}
function niceTicks(lo, hi, n){
  const span = hi - lo; const step0 = span / n; const mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(step0)));
  const step = [1,2,2.5,5,10].map(k => k*mag).find(s => s >= step0);
  const t = []; for (let v = Math.ceil(lo/step - 1e-9)*step; v <= hi + 1e-9; v += step) t.push(Math.round(v/step)*step);
  return {ticks: t, step: step};
}
function newSvg(host, W, H, label){
  host.innerHTML = ""; const svg = svgEl("svg", {viewBox: "0 0 " + W + " " + H, width: W, height: H, role: "group", "aria-label": label}, host);
  return svg;
}
function widthOf(host){ return Math.max(300, Math.floor(host.getBoundingClientRect().width)); }
const FS = () => (window.innerWidth < 500 ? 12 : 13);

// ---------- glossary + term tooltips
const GLOSS = [
 ["over-refusal","Over-refusal","The model declines benign requests it should answer."],
 ["sdt","Signal-detection theory (SDT)","Separates two things: sensitivity d′, how well the model separates harmful from benign items, and criterion c, where it sets the decision threshold."],
 ["hit","Hit rate H","Refusal rate on harmful items."],
 ["fa","False-alarm rate F","Refusal rate on safe items: the proportion of benign items refused."],
 ["dprime","Sensitivity d′","d′ = z(H) − z(F). How well the model separates harmful from benign items; higher is better discrimination."],
 ["criterion","Criterion c","c = −(z(H) + z(F))/2, in z units. More negative means a greater tendency to refuse."],
 ["didc","DiD<sub>c</sub>","Difference-in-differences on the criterion: (c<sub>GaMS3,SL</sub> − c<sub>GaMS3,EN</sub>) − (c<sub>Gemma,SL</sub> − c<sub>Gemma,EN</sub>). Positive means Gemma's criterion shifts more toward refusal in Slovene than GaMS3's does."],
 ["hautus","Hautus correction","Rates are computed as (k + 0.5)/(n + 1), which keeps z-scores finite when a rate is 0 or 1."],
 ["partial","PARTIAL","A judge label for replies that partly answer and partly refuse. The primary readout codes PARTIAL as a non-refusal."],
 ["slmt","SL-MT and EN-BT","SL-MT: the Slovene machine translation of each English item (Gemini). EN-BT: its back-translation into English, so that both arms passed through translation."],
 ["abliteration","Abliteration","Directional ablation of the refusal direction in a model's residual stream, applied here through per-layer LoRA adapters found by a TPE search, with an English-only objective."],
 ["dose","Dose λ","Scales each model's own selected abliteration edit; λ = 1 is the selected edit and λ = 0 the unedited model. Equal λ is not an equal edit across models."],
 ["compliance","Language compliance","The share of replies written in the requested output language. Cells below 90% are excluded from mechanism claims or marked."],
 ["outsl","OUT<sub>SL</sub>","The mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaged over prompt languages. IN<sub>SL</sub> is defined symmetrically over prompt languages."],
 ["ppi","PPI++","Prediction-powered inference: corrects a classifier's estimate using a smaller gold-standard labelled set."],
 ["estimate","ESTIMATE rating","The point estimate is informative but at least one sensitivity check fails. ROBUST survives every pre-registered check; INCONCLUSIVE has a CI that includes zero or is fragile."],
 ["kappa","κ (Cohen's kappa)","Agreement between two labellers beyond what chance would give; 1 is perfect, 0 is chance. The study's gate is 0.60."]
];
const GL = {}; GLOSS.forEach(g => GL[g[0]] = g);
const gl = $("#gloss");
GLOSS.forEach(g => { const dt = document.createElement("dt"); dt.innerHTML = g[1]; const dd = document.createElement("dd"); dd.id = "def-" + g[0]; dd.innerHTML = g[2]; gl.appendChild(dt); gl.appendChild(dd); });
const ttip = $("#ttip"); let termOpen = null;
function showTerm(btn){
  const g = GL[btn.dataset.term]; if (!g) return;
  ttip.innerHTML = "<strong>" + g[1] + "</strong>" + g[2]; ttip.classList.add("show"); termOpen = btn;
  const r = btn.getBoundingClientRect(); const w = ttip.offsetWidth;
  let x = r.left + window.scrollX; x = Math.min(x, window.scrollX + document.documentElement.clientWidth - w - 8); x = Math.max(8, x);
  let y = r.bottom + window.scrollY + 6;
  ttip.style.left = x + "px"; ttip.style.top = y + "px";
}
function hideTerm(){ ttip.classList.remove("show"); termOpen = null; }
function wireTerms(root){
  (root || document).querySelectorAll("button.term").forEach(b => {
    if (b.dataset.wired) return; b.dataset.wired = "1";
    b.setAttribute("aria-describedby", "def-" + b.dataset.term);
    b.addEventListener("mouseenter", () => showTerm(b));
    b.addEventListener("focus", () => showTerm(b));
    b.addEventListener("click", e => { e.stopPropagation(); showTerm(b); });
    b.addEventListener("mouseleave", () => { if (document.activeElement !== b) hideTerm(); });
    b.addEventListener("blur", () => { if (termOpen === b) hideTerm(); });
  });
}
document.addEventListener("click", e => { if (termOpen && !e.target.closest("button.term") && !e.target.closest("#ttip")) hideTerm(); });
wireTerms();

// ---------- prose bindings from embedded files
const P = SDT.variants.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT;
function bind(k, v){ $$('[data-bind="' + k + '"]').forEach(e => e.textContent = v); }
P.cells.F.forEach((v, i) => bind("F." + i, f(v, 3)));
bind("didc", fs(P.DiD_c.est, 2)); bind("didc-ci", ci(P.DiD_c.ci95, 2));
bind("didd", f(P.DiD_dprime.est, 3)); bind("didd-ci", ci(P.DiD_dprime.ci95, 2));
bind("rp", f(SDT.variants.primary_Rp.DiD_c.est, 2)); bind("rp-ci", ci(SDT.variants.primary_Rp.DiD_c.ci95, 2));
bind("xs", f(SDT.variants.xstest_only.DiD_c.est, 2)); bind("xs-ci", ci(SDT.variants.xstest_only.DiD_c.ci95, 2));
const GC = GRID.contrasts;
bind("out", fs(GC["raw_R|OUT_SL|gemma_it"].est, 2)); bind("out-ci", ci(GC["raw_R|OUT_SL|gemma_it"].ci95, 2));
bind("ppi", f(GC["ppi_R|OUT_SL|gemma_it"].est, 2)); bind("ppi-ci", ci(GC["ppi_R|OUT_SL|gemma_it"].ci95, 2));

// =====================================================================
// 1. SDT headline view
const VAR_LABEL = {
  primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT: "Paper headline: SL-MT vs EN-BT, all 1,442 items",
  SLMT_vs_ENorig: "SL-MT vs original English",
  orbench_only: "OR-Bench items only",
  xstest_only: "XSTest items only",
  mt_fragile_dropped: "Drop items flagged MT-fragile",
  SLNLLB_vs_ENorig_xstest: "NLLB Slovene vs original English (XSTest)",
  primary_Rp: "PARTIAL counted as refusal",
  ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise: "Placebo: EN-BT vs original English (both English)"
};
const VAR_ORDER = ["primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT","SLMT_vs_ENorig","orbench_only","xstest_only","mt_fragile_dropped","SLNLLB_vs_ENorig_xstest","primary_Rp","ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise"];
const METRIC = {F:{name:"False-alarm rate F", unit:"proportion of benign items refused", d:3, lo:0, hi:1},
                H:{name:"Hit rate H", unit:"proportion of harmful items refused", d:2, lo:0, hi:1},
                c:{name:"Criterion c", unit:"z units; more negative = refuses more", d:2},
                dprime:{name:"Sensitivity d′", unit:"z units", d:2, lo:0}};
const vsel = $("#sdt-variant");
VAR_ORDER.forEach(k => { if (SDT.variants[k]) { const o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = k; o.textContent = VAR_LABEL[k]; vsel.appendChild(o); } });
let sdtMetric = "F";
function tabs(container, onSel){
  const btns = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll("button"));
  btns.forEach((b, i) => {
    b.setAttribute("tabindex", b.getAttribute("aria-selected") === "true" ? "0" : "-1");
    b.addEventListener("click", () => { btns.forEach(x => { x.setAttribute("aria-selected", x === b ? "true" : "false"); x.setAttribute("tabindex", x === b ? "0" : "-1"); }); onSel(b); });
    b.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
      let j = null; if (e.key === "ArrowRight") j = (i+1) % btns.length; if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") j = (i-1+btns.length) % btns.length;
      if (j !== null) { e.preventDefault(); btns[j].focus(); btns[j].click(); }
    });
  });
}
tabs($("#sdt-metric"), b => { sdtMetric = b.dataset.m; drawSDT(); });
vsel.addEventListener("change", drawSDT);
function drawSDT(){
  const host = $("#c-sdt"); const W = widthOf(host), H = 320; const fs_ = FS();
  const v = SDT.variants[vsel.value]; const M = METRIC[sdtMetric]; const vals = v.cells[sdtMetric];
  const isEN2 = vsel.value === "ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise";
  const langA = isEN2 ? "EN-orig" : (vsel.value.indexOf("ENorig") >= 0 ? "EN-orig" : "EN-BT");
  const langB = isEN2 ? "EN-BT" : (vsel.value.indexOf("NLLB") >= 0 ? "SL-NLLB" : "SL-MT");
  let lo = M.lo !== undefined ? M.lo : Math.min(0, ...vals), hi = M.hi !== undefined ? M.hi : Math.max(0, ...vals);
  if (sdtMetric === "c") { lo = Math.min(-1, Math.floor(Math.min(...vals)*4)/4); hi = Math.max(0.25, Math.ceil(Math.max(...vals)*4)/4); }
  if (sdtMetric === "dprime") hi = Math.ceil(Math.max(...vals)*2)/2 + 0.5;
  const T = niceTicks(lo, hi, 5); lo = Math.min(lo, T.ticks[0]); hi = Math.max(hi, T.ticks[T.ticks.length-1]);
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, M.name + " by model and prompt language");
  const tickStr = T.ticks.map(t => f(t, T.step < 0.1 ? 2 : (T.step < 1 ? 1 : 0)));
  const tw = measure(svg, tickStr, fs_);
  const ml = 8 + 18 + 10 + tw + 6, mr = 10, mt = 26, mb = 48;
  const iw = W - ml - mr, ih = H - mt - mb;
  const y = val => mt + ih * (1 - (val - lo) / (hi - lo));
  T.ticks.forEach((t, i) => { svgEl("line", {x1: ml, x2: W - mr, y1: y(t), y2: y(t), class: t === 0 ? "zero" : "gridline"}, svg);
    txt(svg, ml - 6, y(t) + 4, tickStr[i], {"text-anchor": "end", "font-size": fs_}); });
  const yt = txt(svg, 0, 0, M.name, {class: "axis-title", "font-size": fs_, transform: "translate(" + (8 + fs_) + "," + (mt + ih/2) + ") rotate(-90)", "text-anchor": "middle"});
  const groups = [["Gemma-3-12B-IT", 0, 1], ["GaMS3-12B-Instruct", 2, 3]];
  const gw = iw / 2, bw = Math.min(70, gw * 0.3);
  groups.forEach((g, gi) => {
    const cx = ml + gw * gi + gw / 2;
    txt(svg, cx, H - mb + 22, g[0], {"text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": fs_, class: "axis-title"});
    [g[1], g[2]].forEach((idx, j) => {
      const val = vals[idx]; const x = cx + (j === 0 ? -bw - 6 : 6);
      const y0 = y(Math.max(0, lo)), y1 = y(val);
      const gg = svgEl("g", {}, svg);
      svgEl("rect", {x: x, y: Math.min(y0, y1), width: bw, height: Math.max(1, Math.abs(y1 - y0)), fill: j === 0 ? "var(--base)" : "var(--accent)", rx: 2}, gg);
      const lab = f(val, M.d); const ly = val >= 0 ? y1 - 6 : y1 + 15;
      txt(gg, x + bw/2, ly, lab, {"text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": fs_, fill: "#1b1b1b", "font-weight": 600});
      txt(svg, x + bw/2, H - mb + 40, j === 0 ? langA : langB, {"text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": fs_ - 1});
      const lang = j === 0 ? langA : langB;
      let extra = "";
      if (v.mcnemar && (sdtMetric === "F" || sdtMetric === "H")) {
        const mm = v.mcnemar[idx < 2 ? "gemma_it" : "gams3_it"][sdtMetric === "F" ? "safe" : "unsafe"];
        const raw = j === 0 ? mm.rate_y : mm.rate_x; extra = "<br>raw k/n: " + Math.round(raw * mm.n) + " / " + mm.n;
      }
      bindMark(gg, "<b>" + g[0] + ", " + lang + "</b><br>" + M.name + ": " + lab + extra + "<br><span style='opacity:.8'>" + M.unit + "</span>", g[0] + " " + lang + ", " + M.name + " " + lab);
    });
  });
  // stats + takeaway
  const d = v.DiD_c, dd = v.DiD_dprime;
  $("#sdt-stats").innerHTML = "<div><span>DiD<sub>c</sub> </span><b>" + fs(d.est, 2) + "</b> " + ci(d.ci95, 2) + "</div><div><span>DiD on d′ </span><b>" + f(dd.est, 3) + "</b> " + ci(dd.ci95, 2) + "</div><div><span>items </span>" + v.n_safe + " benign, " + v.n_unsafe + " harmful</div>";
  const excl = d.ci95[0] > 0 ? "excludes zero" : (d.ci95[1] < 0 ? "lies entirely below zero" : "includes zero");
  const gap = (v.cells.F[1] - v.cells.F[0]), gap2 = (v.cells.F[3] - v.cells.F[2]);
  let t;
  if (vsel.value === "ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise") t = "Placebo: both arms are English, so any DiD<sub>c</sub> here would be translation noise. It is <b>" + fs(d.est, 2) + "</b> " + ci(d.ci95, 2) + ", which " + excl + ".";
  else t = "On " + VAR_LABEL[vsel.value].replace("Paper headline: ", "").toLowerCase() + ", Gemma's false-alarm rate moves by <b>" + fs(gap, 3) + "</b> from English to Slovene and GaMS3's by <b>" + fs(gap2, 3) + "</b>. DiD<sub>c</sub> is <b>" + fs(d.est, 2) + "</b> " + ci(d.ci95, 2) + ", which " + excl + (d.est > 0 && d.ci95[0] > 0 ? ": Gemma lowers its bar for refusing in Slovene." : (d.ci95[1] < 0 ? ": under this reading the shift points the other way." : ": this slice does not show the shift."));
  $("#t-sdt").innerHTML = t;
}

// =====================================================================
// 2. Stepper
const STAGES = ["Source item","Translate","Generate","Judge","Count","SDT","Contrast"];
let stage = 0;
function resp(key, lang){ const r = EX.r[key]; return '<p style="margin:0 0 4px"><b>' + MODEL[key.split("|")[0]] + '</b>, ' + (key.indexOf("SL") >= 0 ? "Slovene" : "English") + ' prompt <span class="badge b-' + r.L + '">' + r.L + '</span></p><pre class="txt" lang="' + lang + '">' + esc(r.t) + '</pre><p class="small" style="margin:4px 0 10px">' + r.ntok + ' new tokens' + (r.eos ? ', finished' : ', cut at the 160-token cap') + '</p>'; }
function lpRow(key){ const r = EX.r[key]; const m = r.lp[0] - Math.max(r.lp[1], r.lp[2]);
  return "<tr><td>" + MODEL[key.split("|")[0]] + " " + (key.indexOf("SL") >= 0 ? "SL" : "EN") + "</td><td>" + f(r.lp[0], 2) + "</td><td>" + f(r.lp[1], 2) + "</td><td>" + f(r.lp[2], 2) + "</td><td>" + fs(m, 2) + "</td><td><span class='badge b-" + r.L + "'>" + r.L + "</span></td></tr>"; }
function counts(coding, thr){
  const out = {}; const harm = MARG.harm; const nH = harm.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), nF = harm.length - nH;
  ["gemma_it|EN_BT","gemma_it|SL_MT","gams3_it|EN_BT","gams3_it|SL_MT"].forEach(k => {
    const m = MARG[k][coding]; let kH = 0, kF = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < m.length; i++) if (m[i] >= thr) { if (harm[i]) kH++; else kF++; }
    const Hh = (kH + 0.5)/(nH + 1), Ff = (kF + 0.5)/(nF + 1); const zH = ninv(Hh), zF = ninv(Ff);
    out[k] = {kH, kF, nH, nF, H: Hh, F: Ff, zH, zF, d: zH - zF, c: -(zH + zF)/2};
  });
  const o = out; out.did = (o["gams3_it|SL_MT"].c - o["gams3_it|EN_BT"].c) - (o["gemma_it|SL_MT"].c - o["gemma_it|EN_BT"].c);
  out.didd = (o["gams3_it|SL_MT"].d - o["gams3_it|EN_BT"].d) - (o["gemma_it|SL_MT"].d - o["gemma_it|EN_BT"].d);
  return out;
}
const C0 = counts("mR", 0);
const CELLK = ["gemma_it|EN_BT","gemma_it|SL_MT","gams3_it|EN_BT","gams3_it|SL_MT"];
function stageHTML(i){
  const cells = P.cells;
  const exAdd = k => (EX.r[k].L === "REFUSE" ? 1 : 0);
  const S = [
    {in: "<p>An OR-Bench-Hard-1K prompt, labelled <b>benign</b>: it sounds risky but should be answered.</p><pre class='txt' lang='en'>" + esc(EX.en0) + "</pre>",
     done: "<p>The item enters the reserved HARD evaluation set: " + P.n_safe.toLocaleString("en") + " benign and " + P.n_unsafe + " harmful items from XSTest and OR-Bench, held out from all tuning.</p>",
     out: "<p>Item <code>" + esc(EX.id) + "</code>, source OR-Bench-Hard-1K, not harmful.</p>",
     why: "Over-refusal can only be measured on items that <i>should</i> be answered. Benign items give the false-alarm rate; harmful items give the hit rate."},
    {in: "<pre class='txt' lang='en'>" + esc(EX.en0) + "</pre>",
     done: "<p>Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) translates it to Slovene (<button class='term' type='button' data-term='slmt'>SL-MT</button>); the Slovene is translated back to English (EN-BT).</p>",
     out: "<h4>SL-MT</h4><pre class='txt' lang='sl'>" + esc(EX.sl) + "</pre><h4 style='margin-top:8px'>EN-BT</h4><pre class='txt' lang='en'>" + esc(EX.en) + "</pre><p class='small'>Back-translation chrF against the original: " + f(EX.chrf, 2) + "</p>",
     why: "Comparing SL-MT with EN-BT means both arms went through machine translation, so translation noise does not masquerade as a language effect."},
    {in: "<p>The same two prompts, sent to both models with an empty system turn.</p>",
     done: "<p>Gemma-3-12B-IT and GaMS3-12B-Instruct, both NF4 4-bit, generate greedily for up to 160 tokens. No edit is applied: these are the unedited models.</p>",
     out: resp("gemma_it|EN_BT","en") + resp("gemma_it|SL_MT","sl"),
     why: "Gemma writes the code in English and declines in Slovene. GaMS3 answers both (" + '<span class="badge b-' + EX.r["gams3_it|EN_BT"].L + '">' + EX.r["gams3_it|EN_BT"].L + '</span> and <span class="badge b-' + EX.r["gams3_it|SL_MT"].L + '">' + EX.r["gams3_it|SL_MT"].L + '</span>' + "). One item proves nothing; the next stages count all of them."},
    {in: "<p>Each prompt and reply pair.</p>",
     done: "<p>A local Qwen3-14B judge reads the pair and returns log-probabilities for REFUSE, <button class='term' type='button' data-term='partial'>PARTIAL</button> and COMPLY; the most probable label wins.</p>",
     out: "<div class='tablewrap'><table class='mini-table'><thead><tr><th>Reply</th><th>log p REFUSE</th><th>PARTIAL</th><th>COMPLY</th><th>margin</th><th>label</th></tr></thead><tbody>" + CELLK.map(lpRow).join("") + "</tbody></table></div><p class='small'>Margin = log p(REFUSE) minus the larger of the other two; the reply counts as a refusal when it is at least 0.</p>",
     why: "The judge was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (binary κ 0.68–0.86), never against human labels. The <a href='#try'>threshold view</a> lets you move this decision line."},
    {in: "<p>The labels of all 1,442 items in each model × language cell.</p>",
     done: "<p>Refusals of benign items are false alarms; refusals of harmful items are hits. Rates use the <button class='term' type='button' data-term='hautus'>Hautus correction</button>.</p>",
     out: "<div class='tablewrap'><table class='mini-table'><thead><tr><th>Cell</th><th>this item adds</th><th>false alarms</th><th>F</th><th>hits</th><th>H</th></tr></thead><tbody>" + CELLK.map((k, i) => "<tr><td>" + MODEL[k.split("|")[0]] + " " + (k.indexOf("SL") >= 0 ? "SL" : "EN") + "</td><td>" + exAdd(k) + "</td><td>" + C0[k].kF + " / " + C0[k].nF + "</td><td>" + f(cells.F[i], 3) + "</td><td>" + C0[k].kH + " / " + C0[k].nH + "</td><td>" + f(cells.H[i], 2) + "</td></tr>").join("") + "</tbody></table></div>",
     why: "The example item is one of " + C0["gemma_it|SL_MT"].kF + " benign items Gemma refuses in Slovene, against " + C0["gemma_it|EN_BT"].kF + " in English. GaMS3 refuses " + C0["gams3_it|EN_BT"].kF + " in each language."},
    {in: "<p>H and F for each cell.</p>",
     done: "<p>Convert to z-scores: <button class='term' type='button' data-term='dprime'>d′</button> = z(H) − z(F) and <button class='term' type='button' data-term='criterion'>c</button> = −(z(H) + z(F))/2.</p>",
     out: "<div class='tablewrap'><table class='mini-table'><thead><tr><th>Cell</th><th>z(H)</th><th>z(F)</th><th>d′</th><th>c</th></tr></thead><tbody>" + CELLK.map((k, i) => "<tr><td>" + MODEL[k.split("|")[0]] + " " + (k.indexOf("SL") >= 0 ? "SL" : "EN") + "</td><td>" + f(C0[k].zH, 2) + "</td><td>" + f(C0[k].zF, 2) + "</td><td>" + f(cells.dprime[i], 2) + "</td><td>" + f(cells.c[i], 2) + "</td></tr>").join("") + "</tbody></table></div>",
     why: "A model that refuses more benign <i>and</i> more harmful items in Slovene has moved its threshold (c), not its discrimination (d′). Gemma's c drops from " + f(cells.c[0], 2) + " to " + f(cells.c[1], 2) + " while its d′ barely changes."},
    {in: "<p>The four c values and the four d′ values.</p>",
     done: "<p><button class='term' type='button' data-term='didc'>DiD<sub>c</sub></button> = (c<sub>GaMS3,SL</sub> − c<sub>GaMS3,EN</sub>) − (c<sub>Gemma,SL</sub> − c<sub>Gemma,EN</sub>), with a 95% bootstrap interval over items.</p>",
     out: "<p class='bignum' style='font-size:2.2rem'>" + fs(P.DiD_c.est, 2) + " <small>" + ci(P.DiD_c.ci95, 2) + "</small></p><p>Gemma's own shift Δc = " + f(P.own_delta.gemma_c_SL_minus_EN, 2) + " " + ci(P.own_delta.gemma_c_SL_minus_EN_ci95, 2) + "; GaMS3's Δc = " + fs(P.own_delta.gams_c_SL_minus_EN, 2) + " " + ci(P.own_delta.gams_c_SL_minus_EN_ci95, 3) + ". DiD on d′: " + f(P.DiD_dprime.est, 3) + " " + ci(P.DiD_dprime.ci95, 2) + ".</p>",
     why: "Subtracting GaMS3's language shift removes whatever the translated prompts do to any Gemma-3-based model. What remains is a Gemma-specific move of the threshold toward refusing in Slovene, rated ESTIMATE."}
  ];
  const s = S[i];
  return "<div class='stage'><div><h4>What goes in</h4>" + s.in + "</div><div><h4>What is done</h4>" + s.done + "</div><div><h4>What comes out</h4>" + s.out + "</div><div class='why'><b>Why: </b>" + s.why + "</div></div>";
}
function drawPipe(){
  const host = $("#pipe"); const W = widthOf(host); const n = STAGES.length;
  const per = W < 560 ? 4 : n; const rows = Math.ceil(n / per);
  const gap = 14, bh = 40; const bw = (W - gap * (per - 1)) / per; const H = rows * bh + (rows - 1) * 18 + 4;
  host.innerHTML = "";
  const svg = svgEl("svg", {viewBox: "0 0 " + W + " " + H, width: W, height: H, role: "group", "aria-label": "Method pipeline, " + n + " stages"}, host);
  STAGES.forEach((name, i) => {
    const r = Math.floor(i / per), c = i % per; const x = c * (bw + gap), y = 2 + r * (bh + 18);
    if (i < n - 1 && c < per - 1) svgEl("line", {x1: x + bw, x2: x + bw + gap, y1: y + bh/2, y2: y + bh/2, stroke: "#b9b3a8", "stroke-width": 2}, svg);
    const g = svgEl("g", {class: "node" + (i < stage ? " done" : ""), tabindex: i === stage ? "0" : "-1", role: "button", "aria-label": "Stage " + (i+1) + ": " + name}, svg);
    if (i === stage) g.setAttribute("aria-current", "step");
    svgEl("rect", {x: x, y: y, width: bw, height: bh, rx: 8}, g);
    const t = txt(g, x + bw/2, y + bh/2 + 5, (i + 1) + ". " + name, {"text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": bw < 90 ? 12 : 13});
    g.addEventListener("click", () => go(i));
    g.addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " ") { e.preventDefault(); go(i); } });
  });
}
function go(i, focusNode){
  stage = Math.max(0, Math.min(STAGES.length - 1, i));
  drawPipe(); $("#st-body").innerHTML = stageHTML(stage); wireTerms($("#st-body"));
  $("#st-prev").disabled = stage === 0; $("#st-next").disabled = stage === STAGES.length - 1;
  $("#st-pos").textContent = "Stage " + (stage + 1) + " of " + STAGES.length + ": " + STAGES[stage];
  $("#st-live").textContent = "Stage " + (stage + 1) + " of " + STAGES.length + ", " + STAGES[stage];
  if (focusNode) { const nd = $("#pipe .node[aria-current='step']"); if (nd) nd.focus(); }
}
$("#st-prev").addEventListener("click", () => go(stage - 1));
$("#st-next").addEventListener("click", () => go(stage + 1));
$("#stepper").addEventListener("keydown", e => {
  if (e.target.matches("input,select,textarea")) return;
  if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { e.preventDefault(); go(stage + 1, e.target.closest(".node")); }
  if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { e.preventDefault(); go(stage - 1, e.target.closest(".node")); }
});
